CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 17
(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children, in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the protection of women and children victims of violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the empowerment of women and protection of child victims of violence.
(2) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for Victims of violence.

CHAPTER IX
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 29
(1) Development and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus with duties and responsibilities in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall cover aspects related to planning and implementation.
(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b shall cover aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.
(5) Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically every 3 (three) months.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by giving consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons who are female.
4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs within the Regional territory.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in the emergence of misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible for victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against victims will, is, and/or has occurred.
14. Service is activities and immediate actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
20. Regent is the Regent of Sleman.
21. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.

Article 4
(1) The objectives of protection for women victims of violence are directed to: a. create conditions that support the development of the potential of women victims of violence;
b. strengthen the potential already possessed by women victims of violence; and
c. improve the work skills of women victims of violence.
(2) The objectives of protection for child victims of violence are directed to: a. provide social rehabilitation for child victims of violence; b. reunite child victims of violence with their family and/or environment; and
c. improve the empowerment of child victims of violence.

Article 7
Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 6 shall be implemented among others by:
a. establishing a network in efforts to prevent violence against women;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of women.

NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Economic factors, the social environment, and technological development have a major influence on the increase in such acts of violence. This condition demands that the Regional Government take concrete steps through programs and activities as efforts to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities, and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for violence prevention efforts and protection of child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

5.6.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the only explicit mention of media is in the elucidation of Pasal 7 huruf c: “sosialisasi … dilakukan melalui media massa, media elektronik, dan/atau penyuluhan langsung kepada masyarakat.” This describes channels for disseminating information about laws/regulations, but it does not clearly establish ‘media engagement’ as a stakeholder engagement mechanism (e.g., partnering with media organizations, involving journalists/media as stakeholders, or a media strategy beyond using media as a broadcast channel). The judge treated mere use of mass/electronic media for outreach as sufficient for ‘media engagement’, which is an overly broad interpretation. Since the retrieved passage [5.6-55] contains exactly this limited definition, the error is primarily the judge’s reasoning/threshold rather than missing evidence.

7.1.rationale: The Indonesian text does not specify a dedicated local government (kabupaten/APBD) budget or funding source for implementing the policy. The cited evidence comes from the elucidation of Pasal 26 ayat (2): “difasilitasi oleh Pemerintah Desa … termasuk memberikan pembiayaan…”. This indicates that the Village Government may facilitate formation of forums and may provide financing for those forum activities, but it is not the same as the policy committing/regulating a local government budget line or funding source for the overall program (and it is village-level facilitation, framed as ‘may’, not a clear budget allocation requirement). The judge over-interpreted this as satisfying a ‘local government budget’ indicator, so the discrepancy is best explained by evaluation failure rather than translation or retrieval.
